methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes, initiations, or same-position minutes) be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells and cases are needed to test a single-teammate largest-gainer prediction?
Do the similarity and minutes-based selection rules yield the same teammate, and is the rule fixed before analysis?
Are pre-absence profiles and post-absence gains measured from the same play-by-play-derived initiation records, creating outcome-derived labels?
Which regression-to-the-mean and selection risks affect comparisons of post-absence gains?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned no records, so no earlier study by this project on this question or closely related questions was available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types.
Whether any approach to this question has been tried, failed, or succeeded.
Reliable sample-size, power, or reliability figures for play-type initiation measures from this project.
own_inferences: The stated rule is disjunctive ('closest profile' or 'most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes'), so the test has several possible operationalizations. Choosing among them after seeing results would create forking paths.
With 11 cases, a top-1 teammate prediction has very limited power. Even with 148 spells, spells within a case are not independent, so the effective sample is closer to 11 cases.

Play-type initiation shares are derived from the same play-by-play that defines the gain outcome, which raises label-definition and leakage concerns if the pre-absence profile and post-absence gain are built from overlapping records.
A teammate with the most minutes or initiations is mechanically likely to gain the most absolute initiations after an absence, so a gain-in-share metric may be needed to avoid a mechanical result.
uncertainties: Exact definitions of 'primary types', 'closest profile' and 'largest gainer' are not given in the task statement.
The 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are partial before 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21, so the data version must be frozen before analysis.
Whether the 11 cases are distinct absent players or repeated spells for the same players is not stated.
The number of absences where the absent player had a clear primary play type is unknown.
Whether the glossary and data catalog define initiator and play-type fields as assumed is not checked in this session.

historical_effect.explanation: No historical records were returned, so the decision rests only on the task statement and the data description. The absence of prior work leaves the power, label-definition, and multiplicity concerns unaddressed by any earlier result.

blocking_constraints.text: With 11 cases, a single top-1 teammate prediction has very low power, and spells within a case are correlated, so the effective sample is far smaller than 148.
Initiation profiles and gains both come from the play-by-play-derived possession records, so the pre-absence profile and the outcome may share the same records.
The disjunctive selection rule (closest profile, most minutes, initiations, or same-position minutes) gives several candidate tests of the same claim.
Teammates who gain most after an absence may be those whose pre-absence usage was already trending up or was unusually low, so gains can reflect regression rather than the profile match.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved (retrieve_history returned an empty list), so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. Nothing is cited.

risks.text: 11 cases give very limited power to detect a top-1 teammate effect; spells nested in cases are not independent.
Pre-absence initiation profile and post-absence gain are both derived from play-by-play possession records, risking circularity.
Play-type initiator attribution from play-by-play and possession records may be noisy, lowering reliability of profile similarity and gain measures.
Selecting the teammate with the largest post-absence gain, or the closest profile after seeing results, selects on noise and inflates apparent gains.
Changes in coaching scheme, roster role, injury return, playing time, and lineup context can drive gains independently of profile similarity.
Several selection rules and several play types can be tested, inflating false positives unless the rule and outcome are fixed in advance.
A teammate with the most minutes or initiations may gain the most by default, so a null baseline must be defined before comparing profile-based prediction.
Attribution of initiator and play type in play-by-play data can be wrong, which misclassifies primary types and gainers.
Season-to-season change across 2022-23 to 2025-26 and partial 2025-26 data can change usage environments.
Without a placebo teammate or placebo absence window, an observed gainer pattern cannot be distinguished from generic usage shifts.

design.estimand: As posed, the estimand is ambiguous. The minimum viable estimand is the probability that the teammate ranked first by one fixed, pre-specified profile rule (closest initiation profile, using the stated fallback only if pre-specified) is the largest share gainer in the absent player's top play type, compared with a minutes-only and a random-teammate baseline.
design.unit: Absence spell nested in the absent player (case). Spell-level results are aggregated to the case level for inference.
design.sample: All 11 cases from 2022-23 to 2025-26 with complete regular-season data (playoffs and partial 2025-26 excluded unless pre-registered), restricted to spells that meet a pre-specified minimum absence length and primary-type threshold.
design.power: Not adequate for a single top-1 test with 11 cases. Power must be computed before analysis, and the study should be reported as exploratory unless the effect is large.
design.controls: Pre-absence trend in each teammate's usage, minutes, lineup role, and season effects as covariates. Gains measured as change in share of the absent player's primary play-type initiations, with pre-absence baselines measured on disjoint possessions from the profile construction to limit circularity.
design.falsification: Compare the closest-profile rule with a minutes-only rule and a placebo absence window (same teammates, periods with no absence). If the profile rule does not beat both baselines, the claim is not supported.
design.multiplicity: Fix one primary selection rule and one primary play-type definition in advance. Treat the disjunctive alternatives as secondary and correct for them.
design.decision_rule: Support the claim only if the pre-specified profile rule identifies the largest gainer at a rate above both the minutes-only and random baselines, with a case-level interval excluding the baseline, under the pre-registered design. Otherwise report as not supported or uncertain.
design.data_version: Freeze the regular-season 2022-23 to 2024-25 files and the complete 2025-26 regular season (from 2026-04-13). Exclude partial 2025-26 playoffs and pre-2026-04-13 partial regular-season data unless the analysis is versioned explicitly.

methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells and cases are needed to test a single-teammate gainer prediction?
Which selection and regression-to-the-mean risks affect post-absence gain comparisons?
Is the play-type initiation label derived from the same outcome it is used to measure?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
